tutorial.addition.count_all.title: Putting together
tutorial.addition.count_all.see: Here are two berries. Here is one more berry. Adding means putting them together and counting them all.
tutorial.addition.count_all.model: Now they sit in the frame together. Touch each one as you count: one, two, three.
tutorial.addition.count_all.worked: Two and one more makes three. The plus sign means put together.
tutorial.addition.count_all.try: One berry, and two more. Count them all. How many?
tutorial.addition.count_on.title: Counting on
tutorial.addition.count_on.see: Four berries here, two there. You could count all six. But you already know there are four.
tutorial.addition.count_on.model: So start at four and take two hops: five, six. You never counted the first four again.
tutorial.addition.count_on.worked: Four plus two is six. Start at the bigger number and count on. It is faster every time.
tutorial.addition.count_on.try: Start at five. Take two hops. Where do you land?
tutorial.addition.make_ten.title: Making ten
tutorial.addition.make_ten.see: Seven in the frame. Look at the empty spaces: three of them. Seven and three fill it exactly.
tutorial.addition.make_ten.model: Three more arrive, and the frame is exactly full. Seven and three are partners: together they make ten.
tutorial.addition.make_ten.worked: Seven plus three is ten. A full frame is always ten, so you never have to count it.
tutorial.addition.make_ten.try: Six are in. Four more arrive. Does the frame fill up? How many?
tutorial.addition.teen_numbers.title: Ten and some more
tutorial.addition.teen_numbers.see: One whole frame, and three more beside it. That is thirteen: a ten and a three.
tutorial.addition.teen_numbers.model: The tall bar is the ten. The little squares are the ones. Thirteen is one bar and three squares.
tutorial.addition.teen_numbers.worked: Thirteen plus two is fifteen. The ten stays put. You only add to the ones.
tutorial.addition.teen_numbers.try: Eleven, and two more squares. The ten does not change. How many now?
tutorial.addition.bridge_ten.title: Past the next ten
tutorial.addition.bridge_ten.see: Sixteen already, and four more coming. Watch the second frame fill right up.
tutorial.addition.bridge_ten.model: Four hops from sixteen: seventeen, eighteen, nineteen, twenty. You land exactly on the next ten.
tutorial.addition.bridge_ten.worked: Sixteen plus four is twenty. Ask yourself first: how far is it to the next ten?
tutorial.addition.bridge_ten.try: Seventeen, three hops. How far is it to twenty?
tutorial.addition.tens_and_ones.title: Tens and ones
tutorial.addition.tens_and_ones.see: Twenty-two is two bars and two squares. Three more squares arrive. The bars do not move.
tutorial.addition.tens_and_ones.model: On the line it is the same short walk as two plus three, just further along.
tutorial.addition.tens_and_ones.worked: Twenty-two plus three is twenty-five. Add the ones. The tens only move if the ones fill past ten.
tutorial.addition.tens_and_ones.try: Thirty-one, five hops along. Where do you land?
tutorial.addition.carrying.title: When the ones fill up
tutorial.addition.carrying.see: Sixty-eight, and five more squares. But there is only room for two before ten squares become a new bar.
tutorial.addition.carrying.model: So take it in two steps. Two hops to seventy, then three more. Seventy is the resting place.
tutorial.addition.carrying.worked: Sixty-eight plus five is seventy-three. Go to the ten first. The rest is easy from there.
tutorial.addition.carrying.try: Seventy-seven and nine. Stop at eighty on the way. Where do you finish?
tutorial.subtraction.take_away.title: Taking away
tutorial.subtraction.take_away.see: Three berries. One gets eaten. It is still drawn, with a cross, so you can see what went.
tutorial.subtraction.take_away.model: Taking away is one hop backwards. Three, then back to two.
tutorial.subtraction.take_away.worked: Three take away one is two. The minus sign means something went away.
tutorial.subtraction.take_away.try: Six berries, two eaten. Count the ones with no cross. How many are left?
tutorial.subtraction.count_back.title: Counting back
tutorial.subtraction.count_back.see: Eight berries, three eaten. Counting the five that are left works, but there is a quicker way.
tutorial.subtraction.count_back.model: Start at eight and hop back three: seven, six, five. Same answer, less counting.
tutorial.subtraction.count_back.worked: Eight minus three is five. Start at the big number and walk backwards.
tutorial.subtraction.count_back.try: Start at nine. Hop back four. Where do you stop?
tutorial.subtraction.bridge_back.title: Back through ten
tutorial.subtraction.bridge_back.see: Thirteen berries, five eaten. That is a long way to count back one at a time.
tutorial.subtraction.bridge_back.model: So stop at ten on the way. Three hops down to ten, then two more. Ten is easy to think from.
tutorial.subtraction.bridge_back.worked: Thirteen minus five is eight. Go down to ten first, then take the rest.
tutorial.subtraction.bridge_back.try: Fourteen, six back. Stop at ten on the way. Where do you finish?
tutorial.subtraction.teens_back.title: Taking a big bite
tutorial.subtraction.teens_back.see: Sixteen: a full frame and six more. When you take away eight, the whole second row goes and more besides.
tutorial.subtraction.teens_back.model: Six hops brings you to ten. Two more takes you to eight. Six and two is the eight you took.
tutorial.subtraction.teens_back.worked: Sixteen minus eight is eight. Break the eight into what gets you to ten, and what is left.
tutorial.subtraction.teens_back.try: Seventeen, eight back, stopping at ten. Where do you land?
tutorial.subtraction.tens_and_ones.title: Taking from the ones
tutorial.subtraction.tens_and_ones.see: Twenty-four is two bars and four squares. Take three squares. The bars are untouched.
tutorial.subtraction.tens_and_ones.model: Three small hops back, and you are still in the twenties. Only the ones changed.
tutorial.subtraction.tens_and_ones.worke: Twenty-four minus three is twenty-one. Take from the ones. The tens only move if the ones run out.
tutorial.subtraction.tens_and_ones.try: Thirty-eight, five back. Where do you stop?
tutorial.subtraction.borrowing.title: When the ones run out
tutorial.subtraction.borrowing.see: Eighty-four is eight bars and four squares. You need to take seven, and there are only four.
tutorial.subtraction.borrowing.model: So take four to reach eighty, then break a bar and take three more.
tutorial.subtraction.borrowing.worked: Eighty-four minus seven is seventy-seven. Down to the ten first, then the rest.
tutorial.subtraction.borrowing.try: Ninety-four, eight back, stopping at ninety. Where do you finish?
tutorial.counting.to_five.title: Counting things
tutorial.counting.to_five.see: Three berries. Count them out loud, and touch each one exactly once as you say its number.
tutorial.counting.to_five.model: The frame keeps them still so none get counted twice. The last number you say is how many there are.
tutorial.counting.to_five.worked: A full row is five. After a while you will see five without counting it at all.
tutorial.counting.to_five.try: Count these. How many are there?
tutorial.counting.to_ten.title: Five and some more
tutorial.counting.to_ten.see: Five in one group, two in the other. You do not need to start from one.
tutorial.counting.to_ten.model: The top row is five. Count on from there: six, seven. Seven is five and two.
tutorial.counting.to_ten.worked: Eight is a full row and three more. Reading the rows beats counting one by one.
tutorial.counting.to_ten.try: A full row and some more. How many are there?
tutorial.counting.ten_and_more.title: Past ten
tutorial.counting.ten_and_more.see: One frame is full, so that is ten. Three more sit in the next one.
tutorial.counting.ten_and_more.model: Thirteen is one ten and three ones. That is what the one and the three in 13 are telling you.
tutorial.counting.ten_and_more.worked: Do not count a full frame. See it as ten, then count only what spills over.
tutorial.counting.ten_and_more.try: A full ten and some more. How many altogether?
tutorial.comparison.more_or_less.title: More or fewer
tutorial.comparison.more_or_less.see: Two on this side, five on that side. You can see which pile is taller before you count either one.
tutorial.comparison.more_or_less.model: On the number line, the greater number is always the one further along.
tutorial.comparison.more_or_less.worked: Ten is greater than eight, because ten comes later when you count. So eight is fewer than ten.
tutorial.comparison.more_or_less.try: Which pile has fewer? Tap the smaller number.
tutorial.comparison.compare_teens.title: Close numbers
tutorial.comparison.compare_teens.see: Fourteen and thirteen. The piles look almost the same, so looking is not enough any more.
tutorial.comparison.compare_teens.model: Put them on the line. Fourteen sits further along than thirteen, so fourteen is greater.
tutorial.comparison.compare_teens.worked: Both start with a ten. When the tens match, the ones decide it.
tutorial.comparison.compare_teens.try: Which number is greater? Tap it.
tutorial.pattern_matching.ab_repeat.see: One, two, one, two. The same two numbers keep taking turns, and the colours show you where.
tutorial.pattern_matching.ab_repeat.mode: Find the part that repeats. Here it is just two long. Then say it again to yourself.
tutorial.pattern_matching.ab_repeat.work: Four, three, four, three, four. After a four comes a three, every single time.
tutorial.pattern_matching.ab_repeat.try: Seven, six, seven, six, seven. What comes next?
tutorial.pattern_matching.longer_core.se: This time three numbers take turns instead of two. Say them once: four, one, six.
tutorial.pattern_matching.longer_core.mo: Now it repeats. Four, one, six, and the four is back. The numbers start over, and so do the colours.
tutorial.pattern_matching.longer_core.wo: After four, one comes six. Count how far along the repeat you are, not how far along the strip.
tutorial.pattern_matching.longer_core.tr: Two, six, four, two, six. Which one takes its turn next?
tutorial.pattern_matching.tricky_core.se: Nine, twelve, sixteen. Bigger numbers, and uneven gaps. You cannot tell what is next yet.
tutorial.pattern_matching.tricky_core.mo: Now you can. Nine, twelve, sixteen, then nine again: those three are the part that repeats.
tutorial.pattern_matching.tricky_core.wo: After nine and twelve comes sixteen, exactly like the first time round.
tutorial.pattern_matching.tricky_core.tr: Sixteen, twenty, twelve, sixteen, twenty. What comes next?
tutorial.number_sequence.one_more.title: What comes next
tutorial.number_sequence.one_more.see: One, two, three, four. This is just counting, written down with the last number missing.
tutorial.number_sequence.one_more.model: Each step is one hop forward. So the next number is one more than the last one you can see.
tutorial.number_sequence.one_more.worked: Three, four, five, six, and then seven. One more, every time.
tutorial.number_sequence.one_more.try: Four, five, six, seven. What number comes next?
tutorial.number_sequence.skip_two.title: Counting in twos
tutorial.number_sequence.skip_two.see: Two, four, six, eight. These jump. Look at the gap between them: it is two, every time.
tutorial.number_sequence.skip_two.model: On the line each step is two hops, not one. Find the gap first, then take it again.
tutorial.number_sequence.skip_two.worked: Six, eight, ten, twelve, and then fourteen. Two more each time.
tutorial.number_sequence.skip_two.try: Seven, nine, eleven, thirteen. Keep the pattern going.
tutorial.number_sequence.bigger_jumps.se: One, four, seven, ten. Still even jumps, just longer ones.
tutorial.number_sequence.bigger_jumps.mo: Measure one gap and you have them all. One to four is three, so every step is three.
tutorial.number_sequence.bigger_jumps.wo: Three, six, nine, twelve, and then fifteen. Add three to the last one you can see.
tutorial.number_sequence.bigger_jumps.tr: Five, eight, eleven, fourteen. What comes next?
tutorial.multiplication.groups_of.title: Equal groups
tutorial.multiplication.groups_of.see: Two boxes, three berries in each. The boxes hold the same amount, and that is what makes this work.
tutorial.multiplication.groups_of.model: Three boxes of two is also six. The same berries, shared out a different way.
tutorial.multiplication.groups_of.worked: Two times three is six. The times sign means groups of.
tutorial.multiplication.groups_of.try: Three boxes, four in each. How many berries altogether?
tutorial.multiplication.tables_small.see: Four boxes of five. You could count all twenty, but counting in fives gets you there faster.
tutorial.multiplication.tables_small.mod: Five, ten, fifteen, twenty. Four times five is twenty, and now you can just remember it.
tutorial.multiplication.tables_small.wor: Three times six is eighteen. Six, twelve, eighteen: three jumps of six.
tutorial.multiplication.tables_small.try: Five sevens. Count in sevens if you need to.
tutorial.multiplication.tables_large.see: Six boxes of five is thirty. Drawing every berry stops helping around here.
tutorial.multiplication.tables_large.mod: So use one you already know. Six fives is thirty, and six sixes is just one more six: thirty-six.
tutorial.multiplication.tables_large.wor: Seven times eight is fifty-six. This one is worth simply knowing.
tutorial.multiplication.tables_large.try: Nine eights. Lean on eight eights if it helps.
tutorial.division.sharing.title: Sharing out
tutorial.division.sharing.see: Six berries, two boxes, shared fairly. Three go in each. Nobody gets more than anybody else.
tutorial.division.sharing.model: Three boxes instead of two, and now it is two each. The same six berries, shared a different way.
tutorial.division.sharing.worked: Six shared by two is three, because two threes are six. Sharing undoes grouping.
tutorial.division.sharing.try: Eight berries into two boxes. How many in each?
tutorial.division.tables.title: Sharing bigger amounts
tutorial.division.tables.see: Twenty berries in four boxes. Five in each, and no leftovers.
tutorial.division.tables.model: Twenty shared by four is five, because four fives make twenty. Every division is a times you already know.
tutorial.division.tables.worked: Twenty-four shared by three is eight, because three eights are twenty-four.
tutorial.division.tables.try: Thirty-two shared by four. Which times fact gives you thirty-two?
tutorial.division.larger.title: Big shares
tutorial.division.larger.see: Twenty-one in three boxes is seven each. The boxes are getting too full to count.
tutorial.division.larger.model: So stop counting and start asking. Twenty-one shared by three is seven, because three sevens are twenty-one.
tutorial.division.larger.worked: Fifty-four shared by six is nine. Six nines are fifty-four, so nine is the answer.
tutorial.division.larger.try: Sixty shared by six. How many sixes make sixty?
math.hint.rel.how_many_more: You have {known}. How many more to make {total}?
math.hint.rel.count_up: Something and {known} makes {total}. Start at {known} and count up to {total}.
math.hint.rel.other_part: {total} is the whole, and {known} is one part. What is the other part?
tutorial.addition.missing_part.title: The hidden part
tutorial.addition.missing_part.see: Eight altogether. You can see five. The question mark is the rest: they are there, you just have to work out how many.
tutorial.addition.missing_part.model: Start at the five you can see and count up until you reach eight. Three hops. Three is the hidden part.
tutorial.addition.missing_part.worked: Five and three make eight, so the question mark was a three all along. Counting up is how you find a part.
tutorial.addition.missing_part.try: Ten altogether, six of them here. Count up from six. How many are hidden?
tutorial.addition.balance.title: Both sides the same
tutorial.addition.balance.see: The same eight, the same five, the same hidden part. Nothing about the amounts changes when the writing changes.
tutorial.addition.balance.model: Now the whole is written first: eight is five and three. Equals does not mean work it out. It means both sides match.
tutorial.addition.balance.worked: Nine is four and five. Four and five is nine. Read it either way round and it is the same true thing.
tutorial.addition.balance.try: Nine is four and something. What has to go in the gap to keep both sides the same?
tutorial.comparison.compare_larger.title: Longer numbers
tutorial.comparison.compare_larger.see: 44 and 99. Both have two digits, so counting digits does not decide it. Look at the left digit first.
tutorial.comparison.compare_larger.model: On the line, 99 sits much further along. Greater still means further, however long the number gets.
tutorial.comparison.compare_larger.worke: 142 against 176. The hundreds match, so move right: four tens against seven tens.
tutorial.comparison.compare_larger.try: 512 or 550. Same hundreds. Compare the tens. Which is greater?
tutorial.number_sequence.big_skips.title: Big skips
tutorial.number_sequence.big_skips.see: 150, 160, 170, 180. Big numbers, but the jump between them is small and always the same.
tutorial.number_sequence.big_skips.model: Measure one gap and you have them all. 180 plus ten is 190. Only the tens digit moves.
tutorial.number_sequence.big_skips.worke: 268, 278, 288, 298, then 308. Ten more each time, straight past the hundred.
tutorial.number_sequence.big_skips.try: 391, 416, 441, 466. Find the gap once, then take it again.
